text:
erica: Quick FYI — NimbusOps wants a tight perf POC. Scope: cold-start tail (p99/p999), sustain 120 qps, short 400 qps bursts (60s), and multi-tenant interference testing. They also want a cost comparison Hosted vs Dedicated.

zara: Clarify traffic shape — is this chat+retrieval or just generation?

erica: Chat with retrieval. Flow: embed (small seq) then 23 chunked generations (~512 tokens).

kyle: Proposed phases: 1) cold boot experiments (10 full restarts) to measure cold p999, 2) sustained 120 qps for 30m, 3) burst to 400 qps for 60s, 4) repeat sustained but with synthetic background tenant noise at 50% and 100%. Also run quantized vs fp16 variants.

zara: Measurement list: p50/p95/p99/p999, token/sec, GPU util, mem pressure, KV cache hit rate, front-door latency (first token wallclock) and server internal time. Capture allocator stalls and any OOMs.

daniel: Load tooling: wrk2 for open-loop gen-only, and a small asyncio driver for embed+chat chaining. Example wrk2: `wrk -t12 -c200 -d180s --rate 120 -s scripts/post.lua http://redwood-hosted/prod/v1/generate`

zara: For chained runs driver will do: embed -> 5ms think -> generate(512). Use 1k unique prompts to avoid synthetic cache bias.

erica: Security check: Nimbus asks if Dedicated supports customer KMS and HSM and whether key material is ever exposed to us. That's a gating item.

kyle: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS integration; Private can offer HSM-backed keys. Will draft a short blurb for the questionnaire.

zara: Cold-start specifics: run node cold (no warmed KV/cache), measure time from request accept to first token, and also model-side startup timestamps. Repeat 10 times to build distribution.

daniel: Pricing roughs for the sales deck: Hosted: usage + burst credits; Dedicated: reserved pool (estimate: ~$45k/month for capacity to keep 120 qps with 20% headroom) — will formalize with finance.

erica: They also want a demo of graceful degradation: fallback to a smaller model if tail latency exceeds threshold. Can we show an automated route that drops to a lighter model?

zara: Yes. Plan a canary where we trigger a route to a ~70% smaller variant when p99 > SLO and show latency + cost before/after. Capture traces.

perf-ci-bot: test-run queued: nimbus-perf-poc-coldstart-1 at 2026-04-10T14:10Z

kyle: Infra checklist: reserve a Dedicated node in staging AZ, enable 10s telemetry scrapes, disable KV-prefix caching for phase1, enable perf profiler around bursts. Also ensure log sampling is off for the short window so we get full traces.

erica: Timeline: kickoff tomorrow morning. Do a quick 10m smoke, then full run next day. Nimbus expects a 24h post-run summary.

zara: Deliverables: 1-page executive summary, p999 CDF figure, throughput vs p99 table, and a short appendix with raw perf logs and config snippets.

daniel: Action items: (1) kyle reserve node + toggle KV flags (2) zara build driver & scripts + deterministic background workload (3) daniel finalize cost delta + questionnaire text (4) erica share prospect security contact and SLA target.

erica: Awesome — looping in their infra lead now. :thumbsup:

kyle: Measurement note: record both wallclock first-token and model internal times. People conflate them often. Also save the cold-start pod logs and container startup timeline.

zara: For comparability, include a deterministic noise run (repeatable background tenant) so we can compare across model builds.

perf-ci-bot: test-run started: nimbus-perf-poc-coldstart-1 (phase1) at 2026-04-10T14:22Z

erica: Perfect. Ill update Nimbus and set the handoff call after the smoke completes.

kyle: If p999 > 2x baseline on cold restarts we snapshot and open an infra follow-up.

zara: Ill post the smoke summary here when ready — short bullet list + one chart.

erica: Thanks team, appreciate the quick turnaround.
